_meta.title: WKU SGA Presidents & Student Regents
_meta.primary_source: Plaque mounted in the SGA Chambers, Downing Student Union 2081, photographed 2026. Transcribed by machine reading of a 4032x3024 photograph, column by column.
_meta.coverage: 1966-67 through 2022-23 from the plaque; 2023-24 through 2026-27 added from WKU News and College Heights Herald reporting.
known_issues: The plaque does not distinguish SGA Presidents from Student Regents. Several years list two names. Some of those are almost certainly mid-year successions; others may be a separately elected student regent. This MUST be resolved before publication - the field 'role' is set to 'unresolved' wherever there is ambiguity.
Three blank plates remain on the wall. Four names are now owed to it.
No name is listed for a full 1974 or a full 2006-07 term.

role_values.president: Confirmed SGA / Associated Students president for the stated term
role_values.unresolved: On the plaque, but overlapping years mean we cannot yet say whether this person was president, student regent, or a successor mid-term

presidents.name: Jim Haynes
presidents.note: First president of the Associated Students of Western Kentucky University, elected 18 May 1966, seven weeks after President Kelly Thompson approved the constitution.

presidents.name: William Menser
presidents.note: A roster of Associated Student Government officers for 1967-68 survives in Kelly Thompson's subject file (UA3/3/1).

presidents.name: Reed Morgan
presidents.note: Single-year plate. Sits between Menser and Straeffer, whose election the Herald reported on 9 May 1968 - so Morgan likely finished a partial term or held the seat between elections.

presidents.name: Bill Straeffer
presidents.note: Election win reported in the Herald, 9 May 1968, in the same issue as an editorial headed 'Elections Illustrate Faults, Indifference'.

presidents.name: Paul Gerard, III
presidents.note: Two-year plate that fully overlaps Straeffer's term. Strong candidate for a separately held student regent seat, or a two-year officer role. Resolve before publication.

presidents.name: John Lyne
presidents.note: Shares 1970-71 with Larry Zielke.

presidents.name: Larry Zielke
presidents.note: Shares 1970-71 with John Lyne.

presidents.name: Linda Jones
presidents.note: First woman to hold the office. The Herald of 28 April 1972 carries a piece headed 'Jones, Linda. Reflects on Term' in the same issue as a strike call over dorm visitation.

presidents.name: Edward Jordan, Jr.
presidents.note: Shares 1972-73 with Michael Fiorella.

presidents.name: Michael Fiorella
presidents.note: Shares 1972-73 with Edward Jordan, Jr.

presidents.name: Steven Yater
presidents.note: No name is listed for 1974-75 as a single term; the next two plates both read 1974-75.

presidents.name: Gregory McKinney
presidents.note: Shares 1974-75 with Jeffrey Consolo.

presidents.name: Jeffrey Consolo
presidents.note: Shares 1974-75 with Gregory McKinney.

presidents.name: Steve Henry
presidents.note: Check whether this is the Steve Henry who later served as Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky (1995-2003). Do not assert the identification without a source.

presidents.name: Christy Mollozzi
presidents.note: A 'Christy Vogt letter' dated 26 April 1977 sits in the SGA document series - possibly the same person under a married or maiden name. Worth checking.

presidents.name: Robert Moore
presidents.note: Three organisation charts survive from 1976-78, so the body was restructuring during this stretch.

presidents.name: Steven Thornton
presidents.note: The April 1979 primary drew 830 voters and put the open-house policy on the ballot.

presidents.name: James Hargroave
presidents.note: Surname spelling on the plaque is HARGROAVE. Verify against the Herald before publishing - it may be Hargrove.

presidents.name: David Payne
presidents.note: One of three names attached to 1982. Likely a mid-year succession.

presidents.name: Sandra Norfleet
presidents.note: One of three names attached to 1982.

presidents.name: Jack Smith
presidents.note: Two-year plate. Either re-elected or the plaque compresses two terms.

presidents.name: Mitchell McKinney
presidents.note: February 1985 Herald ran an apathy editorial and cartoon plus a report on 24-hour open house discussions.

presidents.name: Timothy Todd
presidents.note: Two-year plate. A 1987 Herald piece reports a candidate shortage and mentions a Tim Todd race.

presidents.name: Scott Whitehouse
presidents.note: ASG filed a formal reaction to the General Education Task Force proposal in 1988.

presidents.name: Amos Gott
presidents.note: The best-documented pre-1992 presidency in the archive. Signed correspondence survives on extended library hours, the DUC flagpole, the stadium press box and a local pizza vendor dispute.

presidents.name: Heather Falmlen
presidents.note: Presided over the vote to rename the Associated Students as the Student Government Association: passed 7 April 1992, ratified by referendum 14 April, effective that autumn.

presidents.name: Joe Rains
presidents.note: First president to serve under the SGA name.

presidents.name: Donald Smith
presidents.note: Later president of the College Heights Foundation. Interviewed by the Herald in 2022 on what has and has not changed. At least seventeen numbered resolutions survive from autumn 1993 - the fullest single-semester record in the collection.

sources.label: Herald - The making of an SGA president

presidents.name: Tara (Higdon) Howard
presidents.note: Plaque gives maiden name in parentheses - search both Higdon and Howard.

presidents.name: Keith Coffman
presidents.note: Outgoing letters from this period cover the Dogwood Drive crosswalk and student seating at athletic events.

presidents.name: Stephanie Cosby
presidents.note: Letters survive on ice machines in the residence halls, campus safety, food court hours and professors posting office hours.

presidents.name: Leslie Bedo
presidents.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index marked as student regent for 2001-02 - useful confirmation that by this point president and student regent were the same person.

presidents.name: John Bradley
presidents.note: Presided over the 2004 Constitutional Convention that created the three-branch structure. Quoted in Herald coverage of the investigation into his successor-elect.

presidents.name: Patti Johnson
presidents.note: IMPORTANT: the Herald reported in April 2004 that the president-elect, surnamed Todd, was under investigation over missing SGA dining funds and might resign, triggering a fresh election. Johnson's name on this plate for 2004-05 suggests that is what happened. Confirm before publishing.

presidents.name: Katie Dawson
presidents.note: Named in April 2004 Herald coverage as incoming executive vice president, so she came up through the cabinet.

presidents.name: Robert Watkins
presidents.note: Single-year plate and the only name attached to 2006. No plate covers a full 2006-07 term. Something happened here.

presidents.name: Jeanne Johnson
presidents.note: Overlaps the Johnathon Boles 2008 plate.

presidents.name: Johnathon Boles
presidents.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index marked as student regent for 2008. In office for the February 2008 Frankfort rally, after which roughly fifty senators each filed a written reflection - the richest first-person source in the collection.

presidents.name: Kayla Shelton
presidents.note: Single-year plate; overlaps Kevin Smiley 2009-10.

presidents.name: Keyanna Boka
presidents.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index as student regent, 2013. Plaque spells the first name KEYANNA; the archives index reads Boka, Keyana - confirm which is correct.

presidents.name: Janet "Nicki" Seay
presidents.note: Single-year plate immediately before Nicki Taylor 2014-15.

presidents.name: Jay Todd Richey
presidents.note: Won amid anonymous complaints that he had breached election codes on poster placement. The Judicial Council warned him but confirmed the result stood.

presidents.name: Jay Todd Richey
presidents.note: Re-elected. In office for Resolution 6-17-S, the reparations resolution, which passed 19-10-1 on 18 April 2017 and drew national coverage. Richey publicly framed it as a conversation starter; President Gary Ransdell stated within days that WKU would not adopt it.

presidents.name: Andi Dahmer
presidents.note: Took office alongside incoming university president Timothy Caboni, who began 1 July 2017.

presidents.name: Will Harris
presidents.note: From Glasgow. Sworn in as student regent 2 August 2019. His term ran into the March 2020 campus shutdown.

sources.label: WKU News - regents swear in student regent

presidents.name: J. Garrett Edmonds
presidents.note: The COVID year. Almost certainly the most unusual term in the organisation's history and worth a dedicated oral history.

presidents.name: Matthew Wininger
presidents.note: Sworn in as student regent 6 August 2021, at the meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for Margaret Munday, WKU's first African American student to enrol.

presidents.name: Cole Bornefeld
presidents.note: Elected April 2022 with 49% of 1,448 votes. In February 2023 the Speaker of the Senate brought a censure case against him over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram; the Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure, and a Title IX report seeking his removal was filed two days later. Last name currently on the plaque.

presidents.name: Sam Kurtz
presidents.note: Former administrative vice president. Elected April 2023 on an unopposed ticket with Salvador Leon and Annalise Finch.

presidents.name: Sam Kurtz
presidents.note: Re-elected unopposed. Warned the Senate repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber meant the 2025 election mattered more than usual.

presidents.name: Rush Robinson
presidents.note: Elected 13-15 April 2025 on a turnout of 966. Told the Faculty Senate to 'take a field trip' to see the state of WKU's residence halls. Handed his successor the red suit jacket on 28 April 2026.

presidents.name: Caden Lucas
presidents.note: From Harned. Beat Jaden Marshall in a contested race on a turnout of 1,601 - up 66% on the previous year. WKU Spiritmaster, chair of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, works for the City of Bowling Green's Downtown Development Division. Sworn in 28 April 2026 at the first meeting of the 26th Senate.
